item.title: Even as Trump’s Standing Slips, He Slingshots Darline Graham to Victory
item.description: After facing low approval ratings and endorsement setbacks, the president made a show of force in lifting Darline Graham to the Republican nomination for Senate in South Carolina.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies and Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump hosted a rally on Friday in Myrtle Beach, S.C., for Senator Darline Graham, part of a full-court press on her behalf.

item.title: Graham, and Trump, Triumph: Six Takeaways From South Carolina’s Senate Runoff
item.description: President Trump went all in for Senator Darline Graham in a primary runoff on Tuesday. It worked, preserving his undefeated streak in Republican Senate primaries this year.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Sean Rayford for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham’s victory on Tuesday showed President Trump’s continued ability to move Republican primary voters, especially when he goes all in on a race.

item.title: Joe Manchin Pushes for More Independents to Join Congress

item.media:description: Former Senator Joe Manchin III and his daughter Heather said they believe the door is open given growing public disillusionment with partisan stalemate and party politics.

item.title: As CTE Cases Soar, Why Can’t Americans Quit the NFL?
item.description: A collision of American popular culture and public health is on display in the N.F.L.
item.dc:creator: John Branch
item.media:credit: Mark Makela for The New York Times
item.media:description: According to a new study, about 25 percent of the nearly 900 former N.F.L. players who died between 2016 and 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy.

item.media:description: For parents, the new C.T.E. study layered fear, uncertainty and guilt onto an already difficult situation.

item.title: 5 Takeaways on the Fallout From an Alarming C.T.E. Study

item.media:credit: Kristian Thacker for The New York Times
item.media:description: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy can be diagnosed only posthumously.
